plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks winning and paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I will bid exactly my value of $24 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the market price, and I never overpay since I only pay the second-highest bid. With no prior history to adjust for, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. My value is $16, so I will bid $16.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction with private values. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do—if you bid higher, you risk overpaying; if you bid lower, you risk losing profitable wins. Since this is a one-shot game with no repeated learning needed, I will bid exactly my value of $24 to maximize expected profit.
